# Tusker Docs

Compact catalog of public docs.

- Dispatcher pseudocode | /developer/internals/dispatcher-pseudocode/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-22
  Reference algorithm for a cron-driven binary that turns the vault's dashboard.json into agent runs. This is the contract the Tusker CLI exposes; the dispatcher does not hand-parse markdown.

- Failure classes and recovery table | /developer/internals/failure-classes/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-22
  Every tusker release --to failed|stalled|cancelled takes a --failure-class that drives retry and escalation behavior. The enum is frozen in schema.go.

- Operator intervention | /developer/internals/operator-intervention/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  The dispatcher and tusker CLI cover the steady-state loop. When things wedge — a retry budget exhausts, a human needs to cancel a run mid-flight, or somebody hand-edits a note — a human operator steps in. This doc is the audit-trail contract for those interventions so the vault history stays truthful.

- Orchestration runbook | /developer/internals/orchestration-runbook/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  This is the operator contract for ORC-era agent runs. The current vault note stays the durable work record; runtime state lives in the daemon store and run artifacts. Do not smuggle live process state into frontmatter because that turns markdown into a bad database.

- Tusker V1 Design Index | /developer/internals/v1-design/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-22
  Historical design notes covering the Tusker v1 model and operating assumptions.

- Repository Overview | /developer/repository/repository-overview/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  High-level overview of the Tusker repository, install modes, and key entry points.

- Tusker Spec Set | /developer/specs/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  The implementation spec map for Tusker v2, including subsystem boundaries and build order.

- Spec 00: Product Shape And Operating Modes | /developer/specs/00-product-modes/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  Define what Tusker is before the implementation specs start fanning out.

  Status: Draft

  Status: Draft

- Spec 04: Workspace Manager | /developer/specs/04-workspace-manager/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  Define deterministic isolated workspaces for daemon-run agent sessions.

- 05. Runner And Session Protocol | /developer/specs/05-runner-and-session-protocol/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  Status: Draft Scope: daemon-run execution for codex and claude-code

- Bases — editing and extending | /user/reference/bases/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  The shipped .base files live in assets/bases/ and are embedded into the compiled tusker binary. On tusker bootstrap, they are written to _system/views/ in the target vault.

- Canon locations | /user/reference/canon-locations/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  Tusker supports three legitimate canon patterns. Pick one **per epic**, make it explicit, then create the story stack that executes it.

- Commands | /user/reference/commands/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Full CLI reference. SKILL.md has the five quick commands; this file covers everything.

- Docs publication | /user/reference/docs-publication/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Use this when the user wants project docs, a public docs site, a user guide, release notes, or agent-readable canon. Tusker owns the publication rules. Astro/Starlight only renders the exported tree.

- Formal intake | /user/reference/formal-intake/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Creating a story at risk ≥ medium. This is the ceremony path. Load when the work is a feature, migration, refactor with teeth, or anything with rollout or rollback concerns.

- Optional plugins policy | /user/reference/optional-plugins/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-21
  Core rule:

- Plugin compatibility | /user/reference/plugin-compat/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-21
  The skill works without any community plugins. Everything below is optional.

- Prerequisites and setup notes | /user/reference/prerequisites/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  The primary tusker CLI is now built and run with Go.

- Quick mode | /user/reference/quick-mode/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  The low-ceremony path. Use this for 90% of invocations: logging work, discovering follow-ups, closing things out.

- Repo contract | /user/reference/repo-contract/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-21
  The vault is internal working memory. The repository is still where contributors land.

- Risk and evidence | /user/reference/risk-and-evidence/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  How risk drives ceremony, what evidence each risk tier requires, and who can attest.

- Schema | /user/reference/schema/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Frontmatter is the machine layer. Note body is the human layer. Tusker's Go YAML parser preserves the vault schema cleanly, and Obsidian Properties round-trip without drama.

- Specs as D-notes | /user/reference/specs-as-d-notes/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  Deprecated guidance.

- Story decomposition | /user/reference/story-decomposition/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22
  A design doc is not executable work.

- Triggers | /user/reference/triggers/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  When to invoke the Tusker skill, and when to skip it.

- Workflow | /user/reference/workflow/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Short reference for the story lifecycle. SKILL.md has the full decision tree and commands; this file covers mechanics that agents need while working a ticket.

- Agent Workflow | /user/start-here/agent-workflow/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Operating contract for agents working with Tusker in a markdown-first vault.

- Skill Bundle | /user/start-here/skill-bundle/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-28
  Overview of the installable Tusker skill bundle and how operators use it.
